nodes.sub: Voice Orchestrators + Parallel Subagents — an interactive, free-floating map of how one operator commands a visible, parallel, multi-machine fleet entirely by voice.
nodes.edition: Voice · Parallel Agents · Workflows · Federation · Activity Mesh

nodes.h2: The Bottleneck of Solo AI Coding
nodes.body:
A single chat window with one coding model feels fast — until the work gets real. The moment a task has more than one moving part, the **conversation itself** becomes the bottleneck.

You're no longer limited by how smart the model is; you're limited by how much it has to re-read, how long you wait between turns, and how badly a stray "while you're at it…" poisons everything that follows.

Every message rides on top of the entire conversation so far — the model re-reads a growing wall of history on *every single turn*. And a solo chat is strictly one-at-a-time: three independent jobs that could run at once instead run back-to-back-to-back. Your wall-clock is the **sum** of the parts, never the **max**.

**The core insight:** the limit of solo AI coding is not intelligence — it's *context discipline* and *serialization*. The quiet killer is the cache: each casual detour rewrites the warm prefix and taxes every turn after it.

nodes.caption: Figure 1 · cost scales with history, not with the work

nodes.body:
The fix for serialization is to stop being the thing that serializes. You talk to a **voice orchestrator** — an agent whose entire job is to understand intent, answer you instantly, then *delegate the labor* to background workers. You stay in the conversation. The work leaves it.

"Answer with your mouth, work with your hands."

nodes.caption: The InfiniBot voice terminal — an always-on holo scene. You speak; the orchestrator listens and delegates.

nodes.body: The same orchestrator prompt is wired into **three spawn points** so the experience is identical wherever you start it: the web voice stream `server-voice-stream.ts`, the web CLI bridge, and mobile — all fed from a single source of truth, `voice-orchestrator-prompt.ts`.

nodes.body: **Why this is 10×:** the orchestrator turns your single serial thread into a *dispatcher*. You spend your time deciding *what* matters; the fleet spends its time doing it — in parallel, in the background, off your critical path.

When the orchestrator delegates, it delegates to a **fleet of coding agents**. Four interchangeable backends — `claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, `gemini` — each launched detached, each in its own isolated context. Pick the right brain for each job; run as many as the work demands.

nodes.label: Credit Usage
nodes.caption: Plan-aware tracking across all four backends — Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini — each metered independently.

nodes.body: A solo session carries one enormous shared context that every turn re-reads. A fleet carries **N small, focused contexts** — one per agent — each holding only what its narrow task needs. The bug-fix agent never reads the migration. Because each context is small and topical, each agent's *prompt cache stays warm* for the whole task.

nodes.body: A fan-out is powerful once. A **workflow** makes it repeatable forever. InfiniBot's workflow engine (`src/workflows`) captures a multi-step process as a named recipe an agent — or you — can run on demand, on a schedule, or in an endless loop.

nodes.body: **Why workflows multiply the fleet:** the voice orchestrator dispatches *once*; a continuous workflow dispatches *on a loop*. Pair them and the fleet becomes self-feeding — a daemon that refills the queue so your agents never go idle.

Parallelism inside one machine eventually hits that machine's limits. **Federation** removes the ceiling — a single voice session commands a fleet that spans *every machine you own*.

It's hub-and-spoke: one **master**, many **satellites**. A satellite never talks directly to another — every cross-node call tunnels through the master. The two choke points: `isLocalNodeId` and `forwardGatewayCall`.

nodes.h3: Put each job on the hardware that fits
nodes.body: **Heavy build on the workstation** — the big compile, GPU render, full suite. **Light edits on the laptop** — quick fixes on whatever's nearest. **All from one voice session** — you don't SSH anywhere; the master routes each piece to the right satellite and streams results back to where you're listening.

A fleet you cannot see is a fleet you cannot trust. The **Activity Mesh** is a live, spatial picture of everything the fleet is doing right now — the difference between *hoping* the agents are working and *watching* them work.

nodes.label: Agency World
nodes.caption: The live agency view — running sub-agents, the spawn feed, credit usage and progression all in one glance.

nodes.body: The mesh renders through `agency-world-viz` (the live `ActivityMap` engine). Every running agent is a body on the map. Reach for a tool and the agent physically routes to that **tool sector** and back. Federation links show as **conduits** pulsing as work crosses machines. Idle agents rest in the **concourse** — "busy" and "free" obvious at a glance.

nodes.body: **Trust through transparency:** the mesh makes the whole pattern livable. You delegate aggressively *because* you can audit instantly — fleet-wide at a glance, or one agent down to its transcript and its drift.
Each piece is useful alone. Together they change the shape of a working day. One operator's morning, start to lunch, with every capability doing its job — follow the gold path through the stops.

Coffee in hand, away from the desk: *"Morning — ship the auth fix, write the missing billing tests, start the migration draft."* The orchestrator acknowledges instantly and dispatches. No editor opened. No context re-typed.

A `claude` agent takes the auth fix, `codex` the billing tests, `gemini` drafts the migration — and a fourth, on the workstation node via federation, runs the heavy full-suite build the laptop shouldn't carry.

nodes.label: Morning Board
nodes.caption: The morning board — COMMIT TO ONE THING up top, DRIFT RADAR watching every active project below.

nodes.body: A **continuous workflow** has looped since the agents started — pulling fresh context and queuing the next batch so the fleet never stalls. Agents finish a task and there's already another staged. The queue stays full without anyone tending it.

The migration agent wandered — touching schema it was never asked to. No stopping everything: a glance at the flagged focus modal, then a **voice course-correction** — *"migration agent — drop the schema changes, draft only."* It re-aligns; the other three never broke stride.
Auth fix merged, billing tests green, migration draft in review — three PRs shipped before lunch. No code typed by hand. The leverage came from *orchestration*, not from typing faster.

nodes.h2: Why This Beats Solo AI Coding
nodes.body:
The 10× is not one trick. It's three disciplines that **compound** — each multiplies the others rather than merely adding to them.

**Context discipline** keeps every window small and warm. **Parallelism** collapses wall-clock from a sum into a max — and federation makes the worker pool as large as your hardware. **Visibility** lets you delegate aggressively because you can audit instantly.

nodes.h3: Pricing fit: BYOK keeps cost linear
nodes.body: InfiniBot is **bring-your-own-key** — you connect your own provider accounts and inference is billed to you, at cost, by the provider. No token resale, no per-user inference margin. Every isolated context that *saves* tokens saves *your* tokens — and the credits view shows exactly where each one went.

InfiniBot turns you into the operator of a visible, parallel, multi-machine fleet you command by voice — and pay for at cost. Context discipline plus parallelism plus visibility is compounding leverage. *That is the 10× workflow.*
